outputs.L1: A solar cell module and a method for manufacturing the same are disclosed. The solar cell module includes a plurality of cut cell pieces stacked and connected in series, as well as connectors configured to connect adjacent cut cell pieces in series. The cut cell pieces are obtained by cutting a solar cell, and each cut cell piece includes a front electrode and a back electrode. Each connector includes a first surface configured to connect to the front electrode and a second surface configured to connect to the back electrode. The first surface is provided with alternating first connecting areas and first disconnecting areas, while the second surface is provided with alternating second connecting areas and second disconnecting areas. Projections of the first disconnecting areas onto the first surface overlap with projections of the second connecting areas onto the first surface. The front electrode is configured to connect to the first connecting areas, and the back electrode is configured to connect to the second connecting areas. The solar cell module exhibits improved flexibility, thereby reducing the likelihood of breakage of the grid lines and cells.
outputs.L2: A solar cell module and its manufacturing method are provided. The module comprises multiple cell sections cut from a solar cell, arranged in an overlapping configuration, and electrically connected in series. Each cell section has a front electrode and a rear electrode. Adjacent cell sections are serially coupled by a connector having a first face for connection to the front electrode and a second face for connection to the rear electrode. The first face includes first connection regions alternating with first non-connection regions, while the second face includes second connection regions alternating with second non-connection regions. When projected onto the first face, the first non-connection regions overlap the projections of the second connection regions. The front electrode is configured to join the first connection regions, and the rear electrode is configured to join the second connection regions. This structure enhances the module’s flexibility and reduces the likelihood that the grid lines or cells will break.
outputs.L3:
The solar cell module comprises multiple cut cell pieces that are stacked and electrically connected in series. Each cell piece is formed by cutting a solar cell and includes a front electrode on one side and a back electrode on the opposite side.

Adjacent cell pieces are electrically linked by a connector having first and second surfaces. The first surface connects the front electrodes of adjacent cell pieces, while the second surface connects their back electrodes. Each connector surface includes alternating connecting and disconnecting areas. These areas are arranged so that, when viewed in projection, the disconnecting areas on the first surface overlap the connecting areas on the second surface.

This complementary arrangement allows the connector to maintain reliable electrical connections while accommodating mechanical deformation. As a result, the module has greater flexibility and is less susceptible to stress-related damage, thereby reducing the likelihood of grid-line fractures and cell breakage.
outputs.L4:
A solar cell module is formed by dividing solar cells into a plurality of smaller cell pieces and arranging the pieces in a stacked or shingled configuration. The cell pieces are electrically connected in series so that the front electrode of one piece is coupled to the back electrode of an adjacent piece. This series-connected arrangement provides the desired module voltage while allowing the cell pieces to overlap, thereby using the available module area efficiently.

Electrical connection between adjacent cell pieces is achieved using a connector positioned in the overlapping region. The connector includes alternating connecting areas and non-connecting, or disconnecting, areas. These areas are arranged on opposite surfaces of the connector so that a connecting area on one surface overlaps, at least partially, with a non-connecting area on the other surface. One surface can therefore contact the front electrode of a first cell piece, while the opposite surface contacts the back electrode of the neighboring cell piece, without creating an excessively rigid bonded region.

The alternating connection pattern distributes mechanical stress along the connector and permits limited relative movement between adjacent cell pieces. When the module is bent, twisted, heated, cooled, or subjected to external impact, the non-connecting areas can accommodate deformation and reduce the concentration of stress at the electrode joints. The connector thus maintains reliable electrical continuity while avoiding the stiffness associated with a fully bonded connection.

A manufacturing method may include cutting solar cells into pieces, arranging the pieces with adjacent edge portions overlapping, placing the patterned connector between the overlapping portions, and bonding the connector to the corresponding front and back electrodes. The bonding process may be performed with conductive adhesive, solder, or another electrically conductive joining material suitable for photovoltaic modules. The connected cell assembly can then be encapsulated between protective layers to produce the finished module.

By using smaller cell pieces and a connector with alternating connecting and non-connecting areas, the module can flex more readily than a conventional structure having continuous rigid joints. Stress on fine grid lines, busbars, electrode interfaces, and semiconductor cell material is reduced. As a result, cracking of the cell pieces, separation of the electrical joints, and breakage of grid lines are less likely to occur. The design therefore improves mechanical flexibility, electrical reliability, and long-term durability while preserving efficient series connection among the solar cell pieces.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most frequently used words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, object, place, or idea. We say “the book” when we mean a particular book, or “the sun” because there is only one sun in our everyday experience.

Although it is easy to overlook, “the” gives language clarity and focus. Compare “I saw a dog” with “I saw the dog.” The first sentence introduces any dog, while the second suggests a dog already known to the speaker and listener. With only three letters, “the” helps transform something general into something specific.

Its simplicity shows how even the smallest words can play an essential role in communication.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a flexible solar cell module comprising stacked cell pieces connected in series by a connector with alternating connecting and disconnecting areas on opposite surfaces.
counterfactuals.output: A flexible solar cell module includes a plurality of solar cell pieces arranged in a stacked configuration and electrically connected in series by an elongated connector. The connector has first and second opposite surfaces, each including alternating connecting areas and disconnecting areas. The connecting areas on the first surface are electrically coupled to electrodes of selected solar cell pieces, and the connecting areas on the second surface are electrically coupled to electrodes of adjacent solar cell pieces. The disconnecting areas electrically isolate overlapping portions of the connector from the respective cell pieces, thereby establishing a series current path through the stacked cell pieces while reducing undesired electrical contact. The alternating arrangement permits relative movement between adjacent cell pieces and distributes mechanical stress during bending, thereby improving flexibility and resistance to cracking or interconnection failure.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in formal technical language, a shingled solar cell module design that improves flexibility by using patterned connection and disconnection regions on both sides of an inter-cell connector.
counterfactuals.output:
A flexible shingled photovoltaic module may be formed from a plurality of narrow solar-cell strips arranged in an overlapping, roof-tile configuration. Adjacent strips are electrically coupled by an elongated inter-cell connector positioned within the overlap between the rear electrode of an upper strip and the front electrode of a lower strip. The connector may be a conductive foil, ribbon, mesh, or conductive-adhesive composite extending substantially parallel to the longitudinal edges of the cell strips.

The two opposed surfaces of the inter-cell connector are each divided into a spatially patterned sequence of:

1. **Connection regions**, in which the connector is electrically and mechanically bonded to the corresponding solar-cell electrode; and  
2. **Disconnection regions**, in which no rigid electrical or mechanical joint is formed.

The connection regions may comprise solder, conductive adhesive, metallized contact pads, welded interfaces, or another conductive attachment material. The disconnection regions may be realized as unbonded gaps, recessed portions, apertures, insulating coatings, adhesive-free zones, or locally compliant sections. The pattern may be periodic or non-periodic and may include discrete islands, transverse bands, staggered segments, or other discontinuous geometries.

Preferably, the connection and disconnection regions on the first surface of the connector are offset relative to those on the second surface. Thus, a rigid attachment to one cell does not necessarily coincide through the connector thickness with a rigid attachment to the adjacent cell. This staggered arrangement interrupts continuous high-stiffness load paths across the cell overlap. During bending, tensile and shear deformation can be accommodated by the unbonded or compliant portions of the connector rather than being transferred directly into the brittle semiconductor material or concentrated at a continuous bond line.

Electrically, the multiple connection regions provide parallel current-transfer paths between adjacent cells. The conductive body of the connector maintains longitudinal current continuity across the intervening disconnection regions. Mechanically, the discontinuous bonding pattern permits local sliding, rotation, and elastic deformation within the overlap. The connector therefore functions both as an electrical interconnect and as a strain-relief element.

The dimensions, spacing, and relative offset of the regions may be selected so that the connected area is sufficient to satisfy contact-resistance and current-carrying requirements while the disconnected area provides the desired bending compliance. Region boundaries may be rounded or tapered to reduce stress concentration. The connector itself may additionally include corrugations, perforations, reduced-thickness sections, serpentine portions, or a low-modulus conductive carrier.

Compared with a conventional continuously soldered shingled interconnection, this configuration reduces bending stiffness, interfacial shear stress, cell-edge stress, and the likelihood of semiconductor cracking or bond delamination. At the same time, redundant distributed contacts preserve electrical performance if an individual connection region becomes damaged. The resulting module is consequently better suited to curved, conformable, lightweight, or repeatedly flexed photovoltaic assemblies.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an invention disclosure paragraph for a photovoltaic module made from serially connected solar-cell cutting pieces, specifying front and back electrodes, alternating connector regions, and improved resistance to cracking.
counterfactuals.output: A photovoltaic module is disclosed comprising a plurality of solar-cell cutting pieces arranged in an overlapping or adjacent configuration and electrically connected in series. Each cutting piece includes a light-receiving front surface having a front electrode and an opposite back surface having a back electrode. The cutting pieces are provided with connector regions that alternate between front-electrode connector regions and back-electrode connector regions along the series-connection direction, such that the front electrode of one cutting piece is electrically coupled to the back electrode of an adjacent cutting piece. The alternating connector arrangement distributes electrical and mechanical loads across the module, reduces localized stress concentrations, and maintains current-collection paths when a cutting piece develops a crack, thereby improving crack resistance, electrical reliability, and power-output retention.
